## Introduction

In conversation with Gemini we came up with a possible approach to extend fastICA to find planted binary vectors using the Burer-Monteiro formulation of a semi-definite program. Here I wanted to try out this approach. The code below worked first time for k=20, but for k=40 it fails. I am publishing this before trying something to fix the problem for k=40.


## Code


```{r}
# Set dimensions
n <- 100
k <- 20
p <- 6 # Overparameterization rank (slightly larger than sqrt(k))

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Generate Toy Data (The Projection Matrix)
# ---------------------------------------------------------
set.seed(42)

# Plant a true binary vector
v_true <- sample(c(-1, 1), n, replace = TRUE) 

# Create a random (k-1) dimensional subspace 
X <- matrix(rnorm(n * (k - 1)), n, k - 1)

# Project out v_true from X so the basis is clean
X <- X - (v_true %*% (t(v_true) %*% X)) / n

# Combine v_true and the random subspace to form the raw basis
Basis_raw <- cbind(v_true, X)

# Orthonormalize using QR decomposition to get the n x k basis U
U <- qr.Q(qr(Basis_raw))

# (The projection matrix is P = U %*% t(U), but we only need U for the math)

```


```{r}
# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Define Objective and Gradient Functions
# ---------------------------------------------------------

loss_fn <- function(W_vec, U, k, p) {
  W <- matrix(W_vec, k, p)
  UW <- U %*% W
  row_norms_sq <- rowSums(UW^2)     # Diagonal of U * W * W^T * U^T
  residuals <- row_norms_sq - 1     # Deviation from binary constraint
  return(sum(residuals^2))
}

grad_fn <- function(W_vec, U, k, p) {
  W <- matrix(W_vec, k, p)
  UW <- U %*% W
  row_norms_sq <- rowSums(UW^2)
  residuals <- row_norms_sq - 1
  
  # Vectorized gradient: 4 * U^T * diag(residuals) * (UW)
  # In R, multiplying a vector by a matrix row-wise is done efficiently with '*'
  grad_matrix <- 4 * t(U) %*% (residuals * UW) 
  
  return(as.vector(grad_matrix))
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Optimize using L-BFGS
# ---------------------------------------------------------

# Initialize W randomly
W_init <- matrix(rnorm(k * p), k, p)

# Run the optimizer
opt_res <- optim(
  par = as.vector(W_init),
  fn = loss_fn,
  gr = grad_fn,
  U = U,
  k = k,
  p = p,
  method = "BFGS",
  control = list(maxit = 1000)
)
```



```{r}
# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Extract Solution
# ---------------------------------------------------------

W_opt <- matrix(opt_res$par, k, p)

# Because Y = W W^T collapses to rank 1, W_opt is effectively rank 1.
# The top left singular vector of W_opt is our coefficient vector 'q'
svd_res <- svd(W_opt)
q_opt <- svd_res$u[, 1]

# Project the coefficients back into n-dimensional space
v_est_continuous <- U %*% q_opt

# Snap to binary
v_est <- sign(v_est_continuous)

# The optimizer might find v_true or -v_true (both are valid)
accuracy <- max(mean(v_est == v_true), mean(v_est == -v_true))

cat("Optimization finished with loss:", opt_res$value, "\n")
cat("Recovery Accuracy:", accuracy * 100, "%\n")
```
